# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu

    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
```

  • Compressed Sparse Row matrix (csr_matrix)

Sparse matrices in column format should be stacked horizontally (hstack) , while matrices in row format are stacked vertically (vstack). This tool outputs a single resulting sparse matrix which is compatible with the inputs in format.

Parameters: blocks sequence of sparse matrices with compatible shapes format.

/bin/bash -lc "Rscript - <<'RS'
library(Matrix)
set.seed(1)
obj <- readRDS('tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds')
# normalize counts per 10k, log1p
libs <- Matrix::colSums(obj)
# variable genes using sparse-friendly mean/variance raw normalized approximate
means <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj)
# E[x"'^2]-mean''^2
vars <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj''^2) - means''^2
keep <- means > 0.005
hv <- order(vars[keep]/(means[keep]+1e-6), decreasing=TRUE)[1:3000]
hv_genes <- rownames(obj)[keep][hv]
mat <- as.matrix(obj[hv_genes,])
mat <- t(t(mat) / libs * 10000)
mat <- log1p(mat)
# scale genes
mat <- t(scale(t(mat)))
mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0
pca <- prcomp(t(mat), center=FALSE, scale.=FALSE, rank.=30)
pc <- pca$x[,1:20]
for (k in c(10,15,20,30,40)) {
  km <- kmeans(pc, centers=k, nstart=20, iter.max=100)
  cat('"'k',k,' targets clusters ', km"'$cluster[c('"'Cell_11249_MCI','Cell_10369_WXV')], '\\n')
  print(sort(table(km"'$cluster), decreasing=TRUE)[1:10])
}
# choose k=20 and print marker genes for target clusters
km <- kmeans(pc, centers=20, nstart=50, iter.max=100)
clus <- km$cluster
targets <- c('"'Cell_11249_MCI','Cell_10369_WXV')
for (tc in unique(clus[targets])) {
  cells.in <- names(clus)[clus==tc]
  cells.out <- names(clus)[clus"'!=tc]
  avg.in <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[, cells.in, drop=FALSE])
  avg.out <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[, cells.out, drop=FALSE])
  pct.in <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[, cells.in, drop=FALSE] > 0)
  pct.out <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[, cells.out, drop=FALSE] > 0)
  score <- log2((avg.in+0.01)/(avg.out+0.01)) * pmax(pct.in - pct.out, 0)
  top <- head(order(score, decreasing=TRUE), 40)
  cat('"'\\ncluster',tc,'n',length(cells.in),'targets',intersect(targets,cells.in),'\\n')
  print(data.frame(gene=rownames(obj)[top], avg_in=round(avg.in[top],3), pct_in=round(pct.in[top],2), avg_out=round(avg.out[top],3), pct_out=round(pct.out[top],2), score=round(score[top],2)), row.names=FALSE)
}
RS"

/bin/bash -lc "Rscript - <<'RS'
library(Matrix)
obj <- readRDS('tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds')
libs <- Matrix::colSums(obj)
X <- obj
# log-normalize sparse values by column library size
for (j in seq_len(ncol(X))) {
  if (X@p[j+1] > X@p[j]) {
    idx <- (X@p[j]+1):X@p[j+1]
    X@x[idx] <- log1p(X@x[idx] / libs[j] * 10000)
  }
}
norms <- sqrt(Matrix::colSums(X"'^2))
targets <- c('"'Cell_11249_MCI','Cell_10369_WXV')
for (target in targets) {
  dots <- as.numeric(Matrix::crossprod(X[,target,drop=FALSE], X))
  sim <- dots / (norms[target] * norms + 1e-9)
  ord <- order(sim, decreasing=TRUE)
  top <- ord[1:50]
  cat('\\nTARGET', target, 'lib', libs[target], 'nonzero', length(obj[,target]@x), '\\n')
  print(data.frame(rank=1:20, cell=colnames(obj)[ord[1:20]], sim=round(sim[ord[1:20]],3), numeric=as.integer(sub('Cell_([0-9]+)_.*','\\\\1', colnames(obj)[ord[1:20]]))))
  # top avg genes among nearest excluding target compared to global
  nn <- colnames(obj)[ord[2:101]]
  avg.nn <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[,nn,drop=FALSE])
  avg.all <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj)
  pct.nn <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj[,nn,drop=FALSE] > 0)
  pct.all <- Matrix::rowMeans(obj > 0)
  score <- log2((avg.nn+0.01)/(avg.all+0.01)) * pmax(pct.nn-pct.all,0)
  topg <- head(order(score, decreasing=TRUE), 50)
  print(data.frame(gene=rownames(obj)[topg], avg_nn=round(avg.nn[topg],2), pct_nn=round(pct.nn[topg],2), avg_all=round(avg.all[topg],2), pct_all=round(pct.all[topg],2), score=round(score[topg],2)), row.names=FALSE)
}
RS"

library(Matrix)
obj <- readRDS('tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds')
dn <- attr(obj,'Dimnames'); genes <- dn[[1]]; cells <- dn[[2]]
targets <- c('Cell_11249_MCI','Cell_10369_WXV')
cs <- Matrix::colSums(obj)
# log CPM-ish sparse: scale nonzero x by 1e4/cs then log1p
X <- obj
for (j in seq_len(ncol(X))) {
  st <- X@p[j]+1; en <- X@p[j+1]
  if (en >= st) X@x[st:en] <- log1p(X@x[st:en] / cs[j] * 1e4)
}
# keep variable genes by nonzero frequency and variance approximation
# Use all genes but compute cosine target similarity
col_norm <- sqrt(Matrix::colSums(X"'^2))
for (tar in targets) {
  ti <- match(tar, cells)
  tv <- X[,ti,drop=FALSE]
  dots <- as.numeric(Matrix::crossprod(tv, X))
  sim <- dots/(col_norm[ti]*col_norm)
  sim[ti] <- NA
  top <- order(sim, decreasing=TRUE, na.last=NA)[1:100]
  nums <- as.integer(sub('"'Cell_([0-9]+)_.*','\\\\1', cells[top]))
  cat('\\nTARGET', tar, 'top sim range', round(range(sim[top]),3), '\\n')
  cat('top cells:', paste(cells[top[1:20]], collapse=', '), '\\n')
  cat('numeric summary:', paste(summary(nums), collapse=' '), '\\n')
  # aggregate marker expression among top100 raw counts detection and mean

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.

```yaml
inputs:
```

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis

  set -eu

    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:

    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT

3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# CompBioBench v1: A benchmark of 100 diverse, verifiable questions for agents for computational biology

We introduce CompBioBench v1, a benchmark of 100 diverse tasks for evaluating agentic systems in computational biology. Unlike mathematics and programming, which more readily admit systematic verification, biological data are inherently noisy and open to interpretation. To enable objective evaluation without reducing tasks to prescriptive checklists, we propose a new benchmark-construction strategy based on synthetic/augmented data and metadata scrambling/scrubbing of real datasets to create challenging problems with a single ground-truth answer that require multi-step reasoning, tool use, bespoke code, and interaction with real-world external resources. events.command:
/bin/bash -lc "Rscript -e '
library(Seurat)
full<-readRDS(\"Mouse_SS_Fibro.RDS\")
q<-readRDS(\"tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds\")
cat(\"loaded\\n\")
targets<-c(\"Cell_11249_MCI\",\"Cell_10369_WXV\")
qc<-GetAssayData(full,slot=\"counts\")
# ensure same genes and order
cat(\"genes identical\", identical(rownames(q), rownames(qc)), \"query dim\", dim(q), \"full dim\", dim(qc),\"\\n\")
for(cc in targets){
  v<-q[,cc]
  s<-sum(v); nz<-sum(v>0)
  cat(\"\\nTarget\",cc,\"sum\",s,\"nz\",nz,\"\\n\")
  # candidate by colSums may be memory; compute full sums once
}
fs<-Matrix::colSums(qc)
cat(\"full sums computed\\n\")
for(cc in targets){
  v<-q[,cc]; s<-sum(v)
  idx<-which(fs==s)
  cat(cc,\"candidates total\",length(idx),\"\\n\")
  if(length(idx)>0 && length(idx)<=5000){
    # compare sparse vector equality for candidates
    found<-which(vapply(idx, function(j) isTRUE(all.equal(v, qc[,j], check.attributes=FALSE)), logical(1)))
    cat(\"exact matches\",length(found),\"\\n\")
    if(length(found)>0) print(data.frame(idx=idx[found], cell=colnames(qc)[idx[found]], tissue=full"'$Tissue[idx[found]], clust=full$ClustName[idx[found]]))
  } else if(length(idx)>5000){cat("too many candidates; refining by nz'"\\n\")}
}
'"

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and

2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required

3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.

   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis

    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:

    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

---
name: galaxy-udt-authoring
description: Use when implementing or debugging a fresh Galaxy UDT. Covers GalaxyUserTool representation, input and output binding, command rendering, container discovery and selection, resources, optional runtime probes, and execution failures. Read the bundled implementation reference for concrete templates and failure diagnosis.
---

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

JSON structure report without choosing a metadata member:

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \

  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv
```

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \

  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv \
  meta.data
```

Genome of SARS CoV-2 sequenced from 62 countries (27 groups based on phylogeny) were analyzed for codon usage trend and amino acid composition. Based on the similarity in the pattern of codon usage and amino acid composition among 27 groups, these were further assembled into 3 sub-groups A, B, and C. Groups 1 to 4 formed sub-group A, Groups 5–7 clustered into sub-group B and Groups 8 onward constituted sub-group C. We observed that coronavirus genome in all the 3 sub-groups showed a similar pattern in codon usage with respect to 7 amino acids namely Cys, Glu, Phe, Ileu, Lys, Leu, and Gln with preference towards U/A ending codons. SARS CoV-2 genome of sub-group A showed a tendency to use U-ending codons for 10/11 amino acids except for arginine (AGG). }

events.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > analyze.R <<'EOF'
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Seurat))
x<-readRDS('tissue.fibroblast.q1.rds')
s<-CreateSeuratObject(x)
s<-NormalizeData(s,verbose=FALSE)
s<-FindVariableFeatures(s,nfeatures=2500,verbose=FALSE)
s<-ScaleData(s,verbose=FALSE)
s<-RunPCA(s,npcs=40,verbose=FALSE)
e<-Embeddings(s,'pca')
for(b in c('Cell_11249_MCI','Cell_10369_WXV')){
 d<-rowSums(sweep(e,2,e[b,])"'^2)
 nn<-names(sort(d))[1:60]
 cat('"'\\nTARGET',b,'\\n'); print(head(nn,15))
 a<-GetAssayData(s,layer='data'); av<-Matrix::rowMeans(a[,nn]); bg<-Matrix::rowMeans(a)
 score<-av-bg
 print(head(sort(score,decreasing=TRUE),65))
 write.csv(data.frame(gene=rownames(a),mean=av,bg=bg,score=score),paste0(b,'_neighbors.csv'),row.names=FALSE)
}
saveRDS(s,'analyzed.rds')
EOF
Rscript analyze.R"
